title: Accelerator pool Terraform module: autoscale orchestration, rolling upgrade & health probes
creator: Ravi Patel
description: Create a reusable Terraform module (registry-style) that manages accelerator/ GPU node pools for Private (VPC) deployments with first-class support for both ASG-based and Karpenter-based autoscaling, safe rolling upgrades of AMIs/drivers, and robust health probes suitable for production inference workloads. The module should be opinionated about safety (drain/cordon/eviction windows, maintenance windows), observability (metrics, tags for cost allocation), and cloud-provider IAM least-privilege. Deliverables include module code, example usage, integration tests, CI pipeline changes, and a gradual rollout plan for existing private clusters.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module published under registry path 'redwood/accelerator-pool/aws' with versioned releases
Module supports two operational modes: asg (managed ASG + launch template) and karpenter (provisioner integration) selectable via 'scaling_mode' variable
Safe rolling upgrade workflow implemented: new launch template/AMI can be applied with a 'canary_count' and automatic drain with configurable grace period
Health probe suite included: node readiness (kubelet + driver), GPU driver sanity (nvidia-smi smoke), and runtime KV cache warmup probe; failing nodes trigger cordon + drain policy
Integration tests that spin a small private cluster in CI and exercise scale up/down, simulated driver failure, and rolling upgrade path
Module emits outputs for autoscaler hooks, ASG names, Karpenter provisioner name, instance profile ARNs and CloudWatch/Prometheus metrics namespaces
Documentation and example: terraform usage snippet, migration steps for existing 'gpu-nodegroup' stacks, and SRE dashboard recommended Grafana panels
Security review complete (KMS for AMI encryption, least-priv roles for instance profiles)
implementation_notes: Design choice: prefer pre-baked AMIs when possible for faster boot and deterministic driver versions; provide optional user-data path for cloud-init driver install for experimental regions. For ASG mode we create a launch template with instance metadata tags and a lifecycle hook to run a post-launch healthcheck Lambda. For Karpenter mode we emit labels and taints and a Provisioner manifest via Terraform local file to be applied by the cluster admin. Rolling upgrades are implemented as a two-phase operation: (1) canary replace N instances and validate metrics & smoke tests via a pipeline job; (2) phased replacement using max_unavailable and surge controls. Use terraform 1.5+ features and keep module interface stable: variables for scaling_mode, desired_capacity_bounds, canary_count, drain_grace_seconds, healthcheck_timeout_seconds, maintenance_window_cron. Avoid mutable state in module outputs where possible. Document known limitations: cross-account AMI sharing not handled, and on-prem/hybrid bare-metal is out of scope.

migration_notes: For existing stacks using older 'gpu-nodepool' modules, provide a migration guide: run terraform plan with 'scaling_mode' set to 'asg' and 'migration_mode=drain_and_replace' in a non-production environment, validate telemetry for 24h, then schedule production migration in maintenance window. Keep legacy autoscaling policies until metrics show stable utilization. Provide a migration script 'tf-migrate-accelerator.sh' which automates snapshotting ASG desired counts and creating a canary ASG with new launch template.
testing_plan: Unit tests via terratest for resource creation; integration job in CI that creates a tiny private cluster and verifies: instance launches, GPU driver present (nvidia-smi exit code 0), Karpenter provisioner claims nodes with expected labels, canary upgrade flow passes, and health checks trigger cordon+drain when we simulate driver failure. Add a chaos test to kill the Nth GPU process to validate graceful fallback. Test runs limited to nightly until stability reaches 3 consecutive green runs
rollback_strategy: If rolling upgrade causes regressions, we will abort the upgrade pipeline and re-apply previous launch template/AMI with an immediate scale-up of previous ASG group. For Karpenter, revert provisioner 'instanceTypePreferences' to previous set and cordon new nodes. Create automation to re-provision previous instances within 10 minutes to meet SLOs.
